title: Stress–strain and force–extension behaviour; Elastic strain energy; Progressive waves
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; MT02-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MT02-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; MT02-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MT03-1#N.4, W01-1#N.1, MT03-1#N.8, W01-1#N.15, MT03-1#N.11.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Amplitude
items.clue: Maximum displacement of a particle from its rest position.

items.label: Elastic limit
items.clue: Largest force after which a wire still returns to its original length.

items.label: Hooke's law
items.clue: Statement that extension is directly proportional to the force applied.

items.label: Plastic deformation
items.clue: Change of shape that leaves a permanent extension when the load is removed.

questions.stem: A steel wire obeys Hooke's law. A tension of 60 N gives an extension of 1.2 mm. How much elastic strain energy does the wire store?
questions.explanation: Energy = ½ × force × extension = ½ × 60 × 1.2 × 10⁻³ = 0.036 J.

questions.stem: A loudspeaker plays a steady note to a listener 5 m away in a room with still air. Which of the following travels from the loudspeaker to the listener?

options.text: Energy, passed along by air molecules that vibrate about fixed positions
Air molecules, pushed across the room from the loudspeaker to the ear
Sound particles, which the loudspeaker gives off and the air carries
An electromagnetic signal, which needs no air to carry it across

questions.stem: The spring in a toy dart launcher has a spring constant of 400 N m⁻¹. It is compressed by 0.030 m and then released, firing a dart of mass 0.012 kg horizontally. All the elastic potential energy is transferred to the dart's kinetic energy. What is the speed of the dart?

A vibrator sends waves along a stretched string at constant tension. At 25 Hz the wavelength is 0.80 m. The frequency is raised to 100 Hz. What is the new wavelength, and how long does a wave now take to travel 4.0 m along the string?
questions.explanation: v = fλ = 25 × 0.80 = 20 m s⁻¹, unchanged. New λ = 20/100 = 0.20 m; time = 4.0/20 = 0.20 s, the same as before.

questions.stem: A spring obeys Hooke's law. When it is compressed by 3.0 cm it stores 0.45 J. How much energy does it store when it is compressed by 4.5 cm?
questions.explanation: Energy ∝ (compression)². The compression is 1.5 times larger, so E = 0.45 × 1.5² = 1.0 J.
